query: Identify the material family and primary mechanical property of interest for a study investigating the thermal stability of multiphase alloys under aging conditions. Specifically, formulate a hypothesis regarding whether these alloys undergo a non-monotonic transition in ductility (e.g., ductile-brittle-ductile) and outline the necessary prior evidence regarding their chemical ordering to support this hypothesis. Define the boundary conditions for this transition and propose a falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Multiphase AlxCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys (x=1 to 2) undergo a non-monotonic ductility transition (ductile-brittle-ductile) during aging at 500–700 °C due to the interplay between B2 chemical ordering and sigma phase precipitation. Initially ductile (as-cast), they become brittle upon aging as Cr-Fe enriched disordered BCC regions form and sigma phases nucleate, then regain ductility at extended aging times as sigma phases coarsen and the B2 order partially relaxes.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast AlxCoCrFeNi (x=1–2) eutectic high-entropy alloy with fine lamellar FCC/B2 microstructure; B2 phase is ordered (Ni-Co-Al rich), FCC phase is disordered (Fe-Cr rich).
generation.intervention: Isothermal aging at 500–700 °C for durations ranging from 10 hours to 1000 hours.
generation.conditions: Aging temperature: 500–700 °C; Aging time: 10–1000 hours; Atmosphere: inert (argon); Strain rate for mechanical testing: 1×10⁻³ s⁻¹ at room temperature.
generation.structural_mediator: Evolution of B2 chemical order (loss of order near 1400 °C for x=1, retained for x=2) and precipitation/coarsening of sigma phase (appears after hundreds of hours at 700–1000 °C) and Cr-Fe enriched disordered BCC regions (below 600 °C).
generation.mechanism: Non-monotonic ductility arises from: (1) initial ductility due to lamellar FCC/B2 structure; (2) embrittlement upon aging due to formation of brittle sigma phase and Cr-Fe enriched disordered BCC regions that impede dislocation motion and promote crack initiation; (3) recovery of ductility at extended aging due to coarsening of sigma phase and partial relaxation of B2 order, reducing stress concentrations.
generation.predicted_outcome: Ductility (elongation to failure) will first decrease (brittle transition) at intermediate aging times (100–500 hours), then increase (ductile recovery) at extended aging times (>500 hours), resulting in a U-shaped ductility vs. aging time curve.
generation.baseline: As-cast AlxCoCrFeNi alloys exhibit high ductility (25–30% elongation) due to their lamellar FCC/B2 microstructure.
generation.boundary: Transition occurs only for x=1–2; x<1 alloys may not exhibit the same behavior due to different phase stability; aging temperatures below 500 °C may not trigger sigma phase formation; aging temperatures above 700 °C may lead to complete B2 order loss and different mechanical response.
generation.uncertainty: Exact aging times for ductile-brittle-ductile transition may vary with alloy composition (x value) and initial microstructure; sigma phase precipitation kinetics may be influenced by trace impurities; B2 order relaxation may be incomplete at lower aging temperatures.
generation.falsification_experiment: Perform isothermal aging of Al1.3CoCrFeNi at 600 °C for 0, 100, 300, 600, and 1000 hours. Measure elongation to failure at room temperature after each aging step. If ductility monotonically decreases or increases with aging time (no U-shaped curve), the hypothesis is falsified. Additionally, use in situ neutron scattering to monitor B2 order and sigma phase fraction during aging; if sigma phase does not form or B2 order does not relax as predicted, the hypothesis is falsified.
